_meta.description: Master data file for the InnovateMS Founder Toolkit. Contains all industries, CoPath stages, programs, IP types, investment sources, service categories, and budget benchmarks. Edit this file to update all tools simultaneously.

industries.name: AgTech
industries.description: Agriculture-focused startups, including precision farming, smart irrigation, and ag robotics.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi is the 4th-largest agricultural state by acreage. The Delta region has massive row crop concentration (corn, soy, cotton, rice). Strong opportunity for precision irrigation, drone crop monitoring, yield analytics, and supply chain traceability.
customer_segments: Row crop farmers (corn, soy, cotton, rice)
common_problems: Rural broadband access for IoT sensors
industries.pitch_angles: How do you currently track field performance across multiple acres? What is your biggest input cost and how do you manage it today? What data do you wish you had at planting time?
industries.budget_notes: AgTech hardware prototypes and farm pilots are expensive. Budget for equipment, travel to farms, and a 12-18 month sales cycle with co-ops and large operations.

industries.name: AI & ML
industries.description: Startups leveraging artificial intelligence, machine learning, and automation solutions.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi companies increasingly need AI for back-office automation, rural healthcare delivery, and public sector efficiency. Significant opportunity building vertical AI for underserved sectors where national platforms underserve specific Mississippi needs.
ms_anchors: University of Mississippi Center for Applied Data Analytics
Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians (tech adoption)
industries.pitch_angles: What manual processes cost your team the most time each week? Where do you make critical decisions based on incomplete or delayed data? What would you automate first if you had the resources?
industries.budget_notes: AI/ML startups can bootstrap farther with cloud credits (AWS Activate, GCP for Startups). Major cost is engineering talent. Consider remote-first teams to access talent beyond Mississippi.

industries.name: BioTech
industries.description: Companies working on medical research, genetics, pharmaceuticals, and biotech innovations.
industries.ms_context: University of Mississippi Medical Center (UMMC) is a major research anchor with active commercialization programs. Opportunity in rural healthcare biotech applications, diagnostics for high-prevalence MS conditions (diabetes, heart disease), and pharmaceutical access innovations.
common_problems: Clinical trial recruitment in diverse populations
industries.pitch_angles: What research workflows are most time-intensive for your team? How do you access the patient populations you need for studies? What is your biggest barrier from lab discovery to commercialization?
industries.budget_notes: BioTech has the longest PoC timelines and highest regulatory costs. Budget generously for FDA pathway planning, IP filing, and clinical trial design early. SBIR Phase I ($300K) is often the right first capital raise.

industries.name: CleanTech
industries.description: Renewable energy, circular economy, and sustainability-driven innovations.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi has Tier 1 solar irradiance but limited renewable deployment. Significant opportunity in utility-scale solar, EV charging infrastructure for rural corridors, and energy efficiency tools for large agricultural and industrial operations.
common_problems: Energy cost management for rural businesses
industries.pitch_angles: What percentage of your operating costs are energy today? Have you explored renewable options and what stopped you? What would make switching to clean energy easier for your operation?
industries.budget_notes: CleanTech hardware and infrastructure has high upfront capital requirements. Explore DOE grants, USDA REAP program, and utility partnership pilots to reduce early capital needs.

industries.name: Climate Tech
industries.description: Innovations focused on sustainability, carbon capture, and environmental impact reduction.
industries.ms_context: Gulf Coast vulnerability to climate change makes Mississippi a natural market for climate adaptation tools. Strong opportunity in flood risk modeling, coastal resilience tech, and carbon credit market access for Mississippi's 17M+ acres of farmland.
ms_anchors: NOAA National Data Buoy Center at Stennis
common_problems: Carbon credit market access for farmers
industries.pitch_angles: How are climate events affecting your operations or clients today? What do your customers ask about regarding sustainability compliance? How do you currently assess climate-related risk to your assets?
industries.budget_notes: Climate Tech pilots often require environmental monitoring hardware and regulatory validation. Budget for field testing in Mississippi's extreme weather and Gulf Coast operating environment.

industries.name: Consumer Products & Technology
industries.description: Consumer-facing hardware, software, and e-commerce solutions.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi has a growing entrepreneurial base in consumer products. E-commerce enablement for local brands represents a large underserved opportunity, particularly for Mississippi-made products reaching national audiences through digital channels.
industries.pitch_angles: How do your best customers find you today? What is your biggest challenge getting products in front of online buyers? Where do you lose customers in the purchase journey?
industries.budget_notes: Consumer product startups need to budget for inventory, packaging, and customer acquisition costs. Validate unit economics before scaling ad spend.

industries.name: Cyber Security
industries.description: Startups tackling data security, identity protection, and threat intelligence.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi state agencies, rural healthcare systems, and critical infrastructure face growing cyber threats with limited IT budgets. Strong opportunity for affordable SMB-focused cybersecurity and HIPAA/FISMA compliance tools tailored to Mississippi market needs.
ms_anchors: Mississippi Department of Information Technology Services (ITS)
Mississippi State National Guard Cyber Unit
common_problems: Security talent shortage in rural areas
industries.pitch_angles: What is your biggest cybersecurity concern right now? Have you had a security incident or near-miss in the past 24 months? What security tools do you currently use and what gaps remain?
industries.budget_notes: Cybersecurity SaaS can be capital-efficient with recurring revenue. Invest in SOC 2 or FedRAMP compliance early if targeting government or healthcare — it is a mandatory sales prerequisite.

industries.name: Datatech
industries.description: Big data, analytics, data infrastructure, and AI-driven data solutions.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi's public sector, healthcare, and agriculture generate massive datasets that are largely siloed and underutilized. Opportunity in data infrastructure, reporting automation, and decision intelligence for resource-constrained organizations that lack in-house data teams.
ms_anchors: Mississippi State University Data Science Program
Mississippi Department of Health data division
common_problems: Siloed data across departments and systems
industries.pitch_angles: How long does it take your team to produce a standard report? What decisions do you make without data that you wish you had? Where is your organization's data stored and who can currently access it?
industries.budget_notes: Datatech products often require significant integration work with legacy systems. Budget for a longer pre-revenue period and consider a consulting-led entry to fund early development.

industries.name: Defense Tech
industries.airtable_name: Defense Tech (including Aerospace & Defense, Automotive, Chemical Manufacturing)
industries.description: Includes aerospace, defense, chemical manufacturing, and advanced automotive technology.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi has significant defense presence: Keesler AFB, Camp Shelby, Columbus AFB, and Ingalls Shipbuilding (largest US Navy surface combatant manufacturer). SBIR/STTR is the well-established funding pathway. DoD procurement moves slowly — plan for 18-36 month sales cycles.
common_problems: Supply chain resilience for defense manufacturing
industries.pitch_angles: What procurement pathway would your DoD customer use to buy your product? Have you engaged a program officer at a relevant military branch? Which SBIR/STTR topic areas align with your technology?
industries.budget_notes: Defense startups must navigate complex procurement pathways. SBIR Phase I ($300K non-dilutive) is typically the best first capital source. Budget for security clearances and compliance requirements early.

industries.name: Education Technologies
industries.airtable_name: Education Technologies (including Early Childhood Education, K-12 Education, Higher Education)
industries.description: Innovations in early childhood, K-12, higher education, and corporate learning.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi ranks near the bottom nationally in education outcomes, creating urgency for EdTech solutions. K-12 literacy, rural school connectivity, community college workforce development, and adult re-skilling represent major underserved opportunities with strong federal and state funding support.
common_problems: Rural broadband and device access for learning
Adult literacy and GED completion rates
industries.pitch_angles: What is the biggest learning gap you see in your students or workforce trainees? How do teachers identify who is falling behind and how early? What would a 10% improvement in outcomes be worth to your community?
industries.budget_notes: EdTech sales cycles into school districts are slow and budget-dependent, often tied to federal Title I and Title II funding cycles. Consider B2C or B2SMB entry before selling into large institutional buyers.

industries.name: FinTech
industries.description: Financial technology startups, including payments, lending, and decentralized finance.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi has among the highest rates of unbanked and underbanked residents (~25%). Strong opportunity in financial inclusion technology, small business lending tools for CDFIs, and rural payments infrastructure. Multiple active CDFIs operating in the state.
common_problems: Access to small business credit in rural communities
Loan application and decisioning technology for CDFIs
Mobile payment infrastructure in rural areas
Farm credit and crop insurance accessibility
industries.pitch_angles: What is the biggest barrier your customers face in accessing financial services? How do you evaluate creditworthiness for non-traditional borrowers today? What would make your loan process 50% faster?
industries.budget_notes: FinTech requires significant compliance and licensing investment (money transmitter licenses, FinCEN registration, state banking regulations). Budget $50K-$150K for legal and compliance before launch.

industries.name: Food & AgriTech
industries.description: Expanding AgTech to include food innovation, alternative proteins, and supply chain optimization.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi has world-class catfish aquaculture (largest in US), sweet potato production, poultry processing, and a growing artisan food scene. Opportunities in food safety traceability, cold chain optimization, and locally-sourced food supply chain technology serving Delta operations.
customer_segments: Specialty food producers and artisan brands
common_problems: Food safety traceability and recall management
industries.pitch_angles: Where in your supply chain do you have the most waste or spoilage today? How do you track food safety from source to table? What would make it easier for local producers to access your distribution channel?
industries.budget_notes: Food tech requires rigorous food safety compliance investment. Budget for FSMA compliance, USDA relationships, and cold chain logistics pilot costs. Aquaculture tech has strong USDA grant support.

industries.name: GovTech & Civic Innovation
industries.description: Public sector solutions, smart city initiatives, and civic engagement platforms.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi has 82 counties and hundreds of municipalities, many with limited IT budgets and legacy systems. Strong procurement opportunity via MDHS, MDOT, MDE, and county government channels. State ITS contract vehicles simplify procurement significantly.
ms_anchors: Mississippi Department of Information Technology Services (ITS)
industries.pitch_angles: What citizen service request takes the longest to process in your agency? Where do you still rely on paper forms or fax machines? What procurement pathway would your agency use to buy a solution like this?
industries.budget_notes: GovTech sales are slow and require SLED procurement expertise. Pilot programs with one agency often lead to statewide contracts. Budget for 18-24 month sales cycles.

industries.name: Health Tech
industries.airtable_name: Health Tech (including Telehealth, Rural Healthcare, Healthcare Accessibility)
industries.description: Startups in telehealth, rural healthcare, medical devices, and healthcare accessibility.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi has the highest rates of chronic disease in the nation (diabetes, heart disease, obesity). 47 of 82 counties are Health Professional Shortage Areas. Urgent need for telehealth, remote monitoring, and rural primary care access. Mississippi Division of Medicaid is a major buyer.
customer_segments: Rural critical access hospitals (34 in MS)
Primary care practices serving rural communities
common_problems: Access to specialty care in rural areas
industries.pitch_angles: How long does a patient wait to see a specialist in your system? How do you monitor patients with chronic conditions between visits? What would it take to serve 20% more patients without adding staff?
industries.budget_notes: Health Tech requires HIPAA compliance investment from day one. Budget $30K-$80K for legal and security infrastructure before selling to healthcare organizations. Medicaid reimbursement pathways are worth modeling early.

industries.name: HR & Workforce Tech
industries.description: Hiring platforms, upskilling solutions, and AI-driven workforce management tools.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi faces significant workforce challenges: low labor force participation, skills gaps in manufacturing and healthcare, and high turnover. Strong opportunity in workforce development platforms, apprenticeship management tools, and employer-facing hiring technology.
customer_segments: Community colleges and workforce development boards
industries.pitch_angles: What is your biggest hiring challenge right now? How long does it take to fill a critical open position? What skills are hardest to find in your local labor market?
industries.budget_notes: HR Tech selling to enterprises has long sales cycles. Consider a PLG motion targeting individual managers or teams before selling enterprise-wide to HR departments.

industries.name: LegalTech
industries.description: AI-powered contract management, legal automation, and compliance solutions.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi has significant legal access gaps — rural residents and small businesses often cannot afford attorneys. Opportunity in legal self-help tools, compliance automation for small businesses, and practice management software for solo and small-firm attorneys who make up the majority of the state bar.
customer_segments: Small business owners needing compliance help
common_problems: Legal access for low-income rural residents
Small business contract and compliance management
Employment law compliance for small employers
industries.pitch_angles: What legal tasks do your clients handle without an attorney today? Where do you see the most compliance mistakes from small businesses? What would reduce time spent on routine document work?
industries.budget_notes: LegalTech products must navigate unauthorized practice of law boundaries. Budget for regulatory counsel early and consider partnering with the MS Bar Association for distribution.

industries.name: Logistics & Supply Chain
industries.description: Freight tech, warehouse automation, and AI-driven supply chain optimization.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi sits on critical US freight corridors: I-20, I-55, the Mississippi River, and Gulf Coast ports. Toyota, Nissan, and Amazon have major logistics operations in-state. Strong demand for last-mile rural delivery solutions and fleet management technology.
industries.pitch_angles: What is the biggest inefficiency in your current supply chain? Where do shipments most often go wrong or get delayed? What data would help you make better logistics decisions today?
industries.budget_notes: Logistics tech pilots require access to actual fleet data and operations. Plan for extended pre-revenue periods while doing paid pilots with carriers or shippers to validate the core product.

industries.name: Manufacturing & Construction
industries.description: Industrial innovations, automation, and smart construction technology.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi has a strong manufacturing base: automotive (Toyota, Nissan), shipbuilding (Ingalls), aerospace (Rolls-Royce), and timber. Industry 4.0 adoption is early-stage, creating opportunity for automation, predictive maintenance, and digital twin solutions serving large anchor employers.
common_problems: Supply chain traceability for automotive tier suppliers
industries.pitch_angles: What was your most expensive unplanned downtime event in the last year? How do you currently identify quality issues on the production line? What manual inspection or compliance process takes the most time each week?
industries.budget_notes: Manufacturing tech often requires on-site installation and integration with legacy OT systems. Budget for extended pilot programs (3-6 months) and dedicated customer success resources during deployment.

industries.name: Media & Content Tech
industries.description: Digital publishing, AI-generated media, and VR/AR experiences.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi has a rich cultural tradition (blues music, civil rights history, literary heritage) with underdeveloped digital infrastructure. Opportunity in cultural heritage digitization, local news sustainability tools, and creator economy platforms for Mississippi artists and storytellers.
ms_anchors: B.B. King Museum and Delta Interpretive Center
customer_segments: University media programs (USM, Ole Miss, JSU)
industries.pitch_angles: How do you currently monetize your content or audience? What content would your audience pay for that you do not produce today? How do you compete with free national media for local audience attention?
industries.budget_notes: Media tech products often depend on content rights and licensing. Budget for legal clarity on IP and content agreements early. Distribution partnerships with existing MS media brands can accelerate growth.

industries.name: Mobility & Transportation
industries.description: EVs, autonomous vehicles, logistics tech, and alternative transportation solutions.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi has low EV adoption and limited charging infrastructure, creating first-mover opportunity. Rural transit is dramatically underserved — 40% of rural Mississippians lack reliable transportation to healthcare, employment, or education.
common_problems: Rural transit access for elderly and disabled residents
EV charging infrastructure in rural corridors
Healthcare transportation coordination for rural patients
industries.pitch_angles: How do rural residents without cars access healthcare or employment in your area? What is the biggest logistics challenge for your fleet operation? How many miles does your operation drive per year?
industries.budget_notes: Mobility startups often require regulatory engagement with MDOT, public transit authorities, or utilities. Budget for compliance, permitting, and the long procurement cycles of public sector customers.

industries.name: Ocean Technologies
industries.description: Maritime, naval engineering, and deep-sea exploration tech.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi's Gulf Coast is home to Ingalls Shipbuilding (largest US Navy surface combatant manufacturer), NOAA's National Data Buoy Center at Stennis Space Center, and Gulf of Mexico offshore energy infrastructure. Strong DoD and energy tech market.
ms_anchors: Gulf of Mexico offshore energy operators
common_problems: Oil spill detection and response tech
industries.pitch_angles: How do you currently perform underwater inspection tasks? What environmental data would help you make better operational decisions? What is the biggest safety risk in your maritime operations today?
industries.budget_notes: Ocean tech hardware development is expensive and requires specialized testing infrastructure. Ingalls and NOAA/Stennis partnerships can provide access to testing facilities and initial contracts.

industries.name: PropTech & Real Estate Innovation
industries.description: Smart buildings, digital real estate platforms, and property management tech.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi faces a housing shortage alongside high vacancy rates in smaller cities. Opportunity in affordable housing development tools, rural property market transparency, and property management automation for the state's large base of independent landlords.
common_problems: Property management automation for small portfolios
Rural real estate market data access
industries.pitch_angles: How do you currently track and manage vacant properties in your portfolio? What is the biggest time sink in your property management process? How do small landlords in Mississippi find qualified tenants today?
industries.budget_notes: PropTech products serving real estate professionals benefit from MLS partnership and NAR compliance. Budget for licensing and data agreements with real estate data providers.

industries.name: Retail & E-Commerce
industries.description: Digital marketplaces, direct-to-consumer brands, and retail tech.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi retail has been disrupted by e-commerce, leaving many rural retail corridors struggling. Opportunity in local e-commerce infrastructure, marketplace aggregation for Mississippi-made products, and omnichannel solutions for downtown merchants.
customer_segments: Downtown and main street retail merchants
common_problems: Small brand e-commerce setup and operations
Local product discovery and marketplace access
Rural retail traffic and customer acquisition
industries.pitch_angles: What percentage of your sales happen online vs. in-store today? What is stopping you from selling to customers outside your immediate area? How do you compete with Amazon for local customer attention?
industries.budget_notes: Retail tech selling to small merchants has high churn risk. Focus on solving one specific pain point really well and build switching costs through data and integrations before expanding scope.

industries.name: SaaS
industries.description: Software-as-a-Service solutions across industries.
industries.ms_context: Massive opportunity to build vertical SaaS for Mississippi's dominant industries: agriculture, healthcare, government, and manufacturing — where national platforms underserve specific needs. Lower customer acquisition cost than national competitors because you understand the local context.
customer_segments: State and local government (via ITS contracts)
common_problems: CRM and customer management for non-sales teams
industries.pitch_angles: What software do you use today that you wish did more? What process in your business still runs on spreadsheets or paper? How much time per week does your team spend on tasks that could be automated?
industries.budget_notes: SaaS has the most predictable unit economics of any model. Nail down CAC, LTV, and churn before scaling. ARR milestones of $10K, $100K, $1M are key investor checkpoints in the CoPath journey.

industries.name: Sports & Entertainment Tech
industries.description: Esports, fan engagement, sports analytics, and streaming platforms.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi is deeply invested in college football (Ole Miss, MSU, Southern Miss, Jackson State) with massive fan bases. Strong opportunity in NIL compliance technology, fan engagement apps, and youth sports management platforms for the state's dense network of youth leagues.
customer_segments: University athletic programs (Ole Miss, MSU, JSU, USM)
common_problems: NIL compliance and athlete compensation tracking
Outdoor recreation booking and guide services
Sports analytics for high school programs
industries.pitch_angles: How do you currently manage communications with fans, athletes, or parents? What is the most manual process in running your athletic program? How are you thinking about NIL opportunities for your athletes?
industries.budget_notes: Sports tech has seasonal revenue patterns tied to athletic calendars. Plan cash flow around these cycles and build annual contract structures that smooth revenue.

industries.name: Web3
industries.description: Blockchain-based startups, including NFTs, decentralized apps, and crypto solutions.
industries.ms_context: Web3 adoption in Mississippi is early-stage, but there is real potential in supply chain traceability (agriculture, timber, seafood) and digital identity solutions for underbanked populations. Approach with strong use-case specificity — solutions in search of problems face tough investor scrutiny.
customer_segments: Gulf Coast seafood and fisheries industry
common_problems: Fraud reduction in government benefits systems
industries.pitch_angles: How do you currently prove where your product came from? Where do you see fraud or trust issues in your supply chain? What would tokenized ownership or community investment mean for your business model?
industries.budget_notes: Web3 startups must budget for smart contract audits ($20K-$100K), regulatory counsel on token classification, and community building. Infrastructure costs vary widely by chain choice.

industries.name: Other Industry
industries.description: Startups that do not fit into the above categories but offer innovative solutions.
industries.ms_context: Mississippi welcomes innovative ventures across all industries. If your company does not fit neatly into a category above, InnovateMS can still help. Contact us to discuss how your venture maps to our CoPath framework and available programs.
common_problems: Validating an entirely new market category
Finding comparable benchmarks and TAM data
Educating investors on a novel category
industries.pitch_angles: Who are the customers who experience this problem most acutely? What are they doing today instead of using your product? How would they discover and evaluate a solution like yours?
industries.budget_notes: Without comparable market data, budget conservatively and focus on reaching your first paying customer as quickly as possible. Proof of payment is the most important early signal.

copath_stages.name: Awareness & Lead Capture
copath_stages.label: Stage 0 — Awareness & Lead Capture
copath_stages.tagline: You have an idea — let us confirm the problem is real.
copath_stages.description: Initial founder engagement and basic information gathering. You are exploring whether your idea is worth pursuing.
copath_stages.investment_focus: Personal savings, friends and family, small grants
priorities: Talk to 10+ potential customers before building anything
Define the problem you are solving in one clear sentence
Identify who experiences this problem most acutely
Resist the urge to build — your job right now is to listen
Document every customer conversation, even informal ones

tool_tips.discovery: You are at the very beginning — perfect time to talk to customers. Your only job is to listen, not pitch. Keep your solution idea to yourself for now.
tool_tips.mvp: Too early for feature prioritization. Run at least 10 customer discovery interviews before scoping your first build.
tool_tips.budget: Budget for exploration only: $0-$5K for customer discovery, basic tools, and your first prototype experiment.
tool_tips.plan: Write a simple problem and solution hypothesis — not a full business plan. One page maximum.
tool_tips.competitive: Map the landscape to understand what alternatives your customer already uses today.

key_milestones: Validate problem statement with multiple people saying the same thing
Identify initial target customer segment clearly

copath_stages.name: Intake & Triage
copath_stages.label: Stage 1 — Intake & Triage
copath_stages.tagline: You have confirmed the problem — now confirm the market.
copath_stages.description: Formal engagement with InnovateMS. Triage to understand fit, readiness, and next steps in the CoPath journey.
copath_stages.investment_focus: Friends and family, accelerator and incubator programs, early grants
priorities: Document findings from customer discovery conversations
Identify your beachhead (most specific) market segment
Assess team strength and identify key gaps
Determine if you have a technology, service, or product business
Commit to a problem worth solving before committing to a solution

tool_tips.discovery: You have had some informal conversations. Now get structured. This guide helps you go deeper than small talk and start building real evidence.
tool_tips.mvp: List the minimum set of features your first customer would need to say I need this now. Nothing more.
tool_tips.budget: Budget for PoC work: typically $5K-$25K depending on industry. Do not hire before you have a paying customer.
tool_tips.plan: Your one-pager should clearly articulate the problem, solution, and target customer. Keep it to one page.
tool_tips.competitive: Who are your top 3 competitors? Why would a customer choose you over them today?

key_milestones: Define target customer clearly in one sentence
Map competitive landscape with real competitors

copath_stages.name: Proof of Concept
copath_stages.label: Stage 2 — Proof of Concept
copath_stages.tagline: You have validated the idea — now build the proof.
copath_stages.description: Build a functional prototype and test with real customers. Confirm the core value proposition works in the real world.
copath_stages.investment_focus: Grants, InvestMS Seed Fund, angel investors, CoBuilders and FoundersPlus accelerators
priorities: Build a working prototype — not perfect, just working
Get your first paying customers or signed letters of intent
Begin legal entity formation (LLC or C-Corp)
Document your IP strategy (what do you own?)
Define your revenue model and price point clearly

tool_tips.discovery: You are building something. Resist the urge to show it first — start every interview understanding the problem deeply, then introduce your solution at the very end.
tool_tips.mvp: Use the Impact vs. Effort matrix to ruthlessly cut scope. Ship the core value loop first, everything else is distraction.
tool_tips.budget: PoC budgets range $10K-$75K. Include dev, legal formation, and first customer acquisition costs.
tool_tips.plan: You have data to back up your claims now. This is the time for a real investor-ready one-pager.
tool_tips.competitive: How does your prototype compare on the dimensions your customers care most about? Ask them directly.

key_milestones: Working prototype complete and in customers hands

copath_stages.name: Pre-Seed
copath_stages.label: Stage 3 — Pre-Seed
copath_stages.tagline: You have proof — now build the growth machine.
copath_stages.description: Refine the MVP, prove repeatable customer acquisition, and prepare for your first formal fundraise.
copath_stages.investment_focus: InvestMS programs, angel investors via Mississippi Angel Network, seed funds, crowdfunding
priorities: Achieve repeatable customer acquisition — prove it is not just luck
Prove your revenue model with real paying customers
Build 3-year financial projections with monthly detail for year one
Prepare investor pitch deck (problem, solution, market, traction, team, ask)
Formalize team equity, vesting schedules, and roles

tool_tips.discovery: Focus on retention and expansion. Why do customers stay? What would make them leave? This is now your most important question.
tool_tips.mvp: Build Next features that drive retention and expansion revenue, not features that attract new customers.
tool_tips.budget: Pre-seed operating budgets run $75K-$500K per year. Model your monthly burn rate carefully and know exactly how many months of runway you have.
tool_tips.plan: Investors want traction data. Include ARR, customer count, and month-over-month growth rate in your one-pager.
tool_tips.competitive: Define your defensible moat. Why cannot competitors copy your model in 6 months? Be honest.

key_milestones: Unit economics defined (CAC, LTV, payback period)
Financial model built out to 36 months

copath_stages.name: Seed Round
copath_stages.label: Stage 4 — Seed Round
copath_stages.tagline: You have traction — now scale the growth engine.
copath_stages.description: Raise seed capital, scale the team, and prove scalable growth metrics that justify a Series A.
copath_stages.investment_focus: Seed funds, Mississippi Angel Network, InvestMS Angel Pitch events, SBIR/STTR
priorities: Close seed round ($250K-$2M) with clear milestone plan
Build core team with sector-specific domain hires
Establish repeatable sales process with CRM and documented playbook
Set up board of directors and investor relations cadence
Expand to additional customer segments with validated ICP

tool_tips.discovery: Never stop talking to customers. Your biggest scale-up risk is assuming early customers represent the full market.
tool_tips.mvp: Roadmap features that unlock enterprise deals and expansion revenue from existing customers.
tool_tips.budget: Seed-funded budgets run $500K-$2M per year. Hire aggressively against proven unit economics, not optimism.
tool_tips.plan: Update your one-pager quarterly with current traction data for investor updates and new investor conversations.
tool_tips.competitive: Competitive intelligence becomes strategic now. Know your competitors roadmaps and weaknesses, not just their current products.

key_milestones: Seed round closed with clean terms

copath_stages.name: Series A / VC Funding
copath_stages.label: Stage 5 — Series A / VC Funding
copath_stages.tagline: You are growing — now prove you can dominate the category.
copath_stages.description: Institutional venture capital funding to accelerate growth, expand markets, and build defensible category leadership.
copath_stages.investment_focus: Venture capital, family offices, Mississippi Innovation Fund, institutional investors
priorities: Raise Series A ($2M-$15M) with clear use of funds
Hire executive team — VP Sales, CTO, or CFO depending on bottleneck
Formalize board of directors with independent members
Expand to new geographies or verticals with validated playbook
Develop partnership and channel strategy for non-linear growth

tool_tips.discovery: At this stage, competitive positioning and market size become critical questions. Use interviews to stress-test your market thesis with enterprise customers.
tool_tips.mvp: Platform thinking — features that enable ecosystem integrations, partner channels, and developer extensibility.
tool_tips.budget: Series A burn runs $2M-$8M per year. Hire for scale, not just execution. Every hire should have a clear 18-month impact thesis.
tool_tips.plan: Narrative matters at Series A — story, traction, vision, and team carry equal weight. Investors back the founder who can become the category leader.
tool_tips.competitive: Own your category narrative. Investors back the founder who can convince them this company will be the category leader in 5 years.

key_milestones: $1M+ ARR with strong growth rate and improving margins
Board of directors with independent members formalized

ip_types.name: No Intellectual Property
ip_types.description: No IP protection developed or claimed. Common at Stage 0-1.

ip_types.name: Trade Secret
ip_types.description: Confidential business info protected by secrecy — formulas, processes, customer lists.

ip_types.name: Copyrights
ip_types.description: Protects original works of authorship: software code, written materials, creative content.

ip_types.name: Open Source Licensing
ip_types.description: Software code made available under open-source license (MIT, GPL, Apache).

ip_types.name: Defensive Publication
ip_types.description: Intentionally published invention details to prevent others from patenting it.

ip_types.name: Provisional Patent
ip_types.description: 12-month placeholder before filing a full non-provisional patent application. Establishes priority date.

ip_types.name: Design Patent
ip_types.description: Protects ornamental design of a functional item — product shapes, user interfaces.

ip_types.name: Full Patent Pending
ip_types.description: Full non-provisional patent application submitted, awaiting USPTO approval.

ip_types.name: Patented
ip_types.description: Granted patent legally protecting the invention from unauthorized use.

investment_sources.name: Personal Savings
investment_sources.description: The most common first capital. Skin in the game signals commitment to future investors.

investment_sources.name: Friends & Family
investment_sources.description: Personal network capital. Simple terms, high trust. Use SAFEs to avoid complex early cap table.

investment_sources.name: Grants (Government & Foundation)
investment_sources.description: Non-dilutive government and foundation grants. InnovateMS can help identify Mississippi-specific opportunities.

investment_sources.name: Accelerator / Incubator
investment_sources.description: Program-based investment with mentoring. CoBuilders and FoundersPlus are InnovateMS flagship programs.

investment_sources.name: SBIR / STTR (Federal R&D Grants)
investment_sources.description: Non-dilutive federal R&D grants for eligible science and tech sectors. Phase I averages $314K. InnovateMS has SBIR resources.

investment_sources.name: Crowdfunding
investment_sources.description: Platforms like Kickstarter, Indiegogo, or Republic. Good for consumer products and community-driven businesses.

investment_sources.name: Angel Investors
investment_sources.description: Individual accredited investors. InnovateMS Angel Pitch events connect founders to local and regional angels.

investment_sources.name: InvestMS (SSBCI)
investment_sources.description: Mississippi State Small Business Credit Initiative capital. Managed by InnovateMS for startup ventures.

investment_sources.name: Mississippi Seed Fund
investment_sources.description: InnovateMS-managed seed fund for early-stage Mississippi companies.

investment_sources.name: Private Capital (Family Offices)
investment_sources.description: Family offices and private equity groups with regional Mississippi interest.

investment_sources.name: Debt (SBA / CDFI Loans)
investment_sources.description: SBA loans, CDFI loans, or revenue-based financing. Good for capital-light businesses with demonstrated revenue.

investment_sources.name: Venture Capital
investment_sources.description: Institutional venture funds. InvestMS and regional VCs active in Mississippi tech ecosystem.

programs.name: FoundersPlus Accelerator
programs.description: InnovateMS flagship accelerator for early-stage Mississippi founders. Equity and non-dilutive support.

programs.name: CoBuilders Accelerator
programs.description: Cohort-based accelerator for Mississippi tech startups. Applications open annually with rolling intake.

programs.name: Mississippi Seed Fund
programs.description: Non-dilutive and low-dilution capital for Mississippi early-stage companies. Managed by InnovateMS.

programs.name: InvestMS (SSBCI)
programs.description: State Small Business Credit Initiative venture capital for Mississippi startups. Federal-state partnership.

programs.name: Mississippi Angel Investor Network
programs.description: Network of Mississippi accredited investors. InnovateMS facilitates pitch events and introductions.

programs.name: SBIR / STTR Resources
programs.description: Federal non-dilutive R&D funding support for science and tech startups. InnovateMS provides application assistance.

programs.name: Partner & Service Provider Network
programs.description: Curated network of vetted Mississippi service providers across legal, tech, marketing, and operations.

programs.name: Mentorship Network
programs.description: Experienced mentors across industries matched to InnovateMS portfolio companies based on sector and stage.

programs.name: Gulf Blue Navigator
programs.description: USM Research Foundation program for late-stage startups. Four-month blended program with access to research, light manufacturing, and funding.
